title: Logical Operators (and / or / not)
summary: `and`, `or`, `not` combine conditions — with a twist: they return one of their operands, not just true/false. That powers defaults like `speed or 16`.

details.heading: What they actually return
details.body: `a and b` → if a is falsy, returns a; else returns b. `a or b` → if a is truthy, returns a; else returns b. `not a` → always a boolean. They evaluate left-to-right and stop early (short-circuit).

details.heading: Short-circuiting
details.body: `player and player.Character` never errors on nil player: if the left side is falsy, the right side is never evaluated. Same for `or`.

details.heading: Luau if-expressions
details.body: For true ternary behavior without the falsy-b trap, use `if c then x else y` — clearer and safer.

explanation.whatItIs: `and` needs both sides truthy; `or` needs at least one; `not` flips. Because they return operands instead of booleans, they double as value selectors.
explanation.whyItExists: Combining conditions is constant: 'alive AND has key', 'use custom speed OR the default'.
whenToUse: Combining checks: `if alive and hasKey then`
Nil-safe chains: `local char = player and player.Character`
Early-out: `if not success then return end`
whenNotToUse: Don't build ternaries with `a and b or c` when b can be false/nil — you'll silently get c
Don't over-chain: `a and b or c and d` is unreadable — use real if statements
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
true  and "x"   --> "x"      (first truthy, so second decides)
false and "x"   --> false    (short-circuit: stop early)

nil   or  10    --> 10       (first falsy, take second)
"hi"  or  10    --> "hi"     (first truthy, keep it)

not true        --> false
not nil         --> true
not 0           --> false    (0 is truthy!)
```
tips: `x or default` is the idiom for optional settings — but remember `false` and `nil` both fall through
When you need 'x unless it's nil', use `if x == nil then x = default end` or Luau's `x :: any` patterns in typed code
commonMistakes: The classic ternary bug: `cond and false or fallback` always gives fallback
Forgetting short-circuit runs left-to-right — put the cheap/safe check first
Using `&&` / `||` / `!` — those don't exist in Luau

examples.title: Defaults and nil-safety
examples.code:
local config = { Speed = 20 }   -- Jump missing

local speed = config.Speed or 16     --> 20 (provided)
local jump  = config.Jump or 50      --> 50 (default used)

local player = game.Players.LocalPlayer
local character = player and player.Character   -- safe: no error if nil
print(character or "No character yet")
examples.whyItWorks: `or` returns the first truthy operand — a perfect 'fallback' machine. `and` short-circuits, so `.Character` is only touched when `player` exists.

examples.title: The ternary trap
examples.code:
local wantsSprint = false

-- BUG: wantsSprint is falsy, so this gives "walk" either way:
local mode = wantsSprint and false or "walk"
print(mode)   --> "walk" ... even though 'and false' was the point

-- SAFE: use an if-expression
local safeMode = if wantsSprint then "sprint" else "walk"
print(safeMode)   --> walk (correctly)
